### 9. Jina AI Releases jina-ocr-v1: A 3.4B MoE Document Parser With Built-In Speculative Decoding for Low-Budget GPUs

**Source:** MarkTechPost  
**Link:** [https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/09/18/jina-ai-releases-jina-ocr-v1-a-3-4b-moe-document-parser-with-built-in-speculative-decoding-for-low-budget-gpus/](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/09/18/jina-ai-releases-jina-ocr-v1-a-3-4b-moe-document-parser-with-built-in-speculative-decoding-for-low-budget-gpus/)

HEADLINE: Jina AI Unveils jina-ocr-v1: Advanced Document Parsing for Budget GPUs

SUMMARY: Jina AI has launched jina-ocr-v1, a state-of-the-art visual document parser designed to convert various document formats into Markdown. With 3.4 billion parameters and a built-in speculative decoding feature, it offers high performance even on low-budget GPUs, achieving impressive scores on benchmark tests.

KEY POINTS:
- Jina-ocr-v1 features 3.4 billion total parameters, with 570 million active per token.
- The model utilizes a FastMTP speculative decoding head that processes 3 tokens per step while maintaining output quality.
- It achieves a score of 91.14 on OmniDocBench v1.6 and 83.4 on olmOCR-Bench.
- The parser can handle 2.57 pages per second on a single A100 GPU.
- Model weights are available on Hugging Face under CC BY-NC 4.0, with hosted access via Jina Reader.

IMPACT: This release enhances accessibility for developers and businesses needing efficient document parsing capabilities, especially in resource-constrained environments, thereby accelerating the adoption of AI in document management tasks.

This model supports both text and image inputs and features an impressive 262K-token context, showcasing advancements in efficient AI model design.

KEY POINTS:
- Ternary Bonsai 2 27B is a ternary-weight model that significantly reduces memory usage.
- The model maintains 98.2% performance across 20 benchmarks compared to Qwen3.8 27B.
- It supports both text and image processing capabilities.
- The model features an extensive context length of 262K tokens.
- It is released under the Apache 2.0 license, encouraging broader use and development.
